# Open-Weight Models

Open-weight models publish their weights so anyone can run, fine-tune, and study them. Releases from DeepSeek, Qwen, Zhipu GLM, Moonshot Kimi, Mistral and others often close the gap with closed models within months.

This page tracks each release we covered, with benchmark results and practical notes on running them.

## Timeline

### October 2026

1. Oct 11

   [OpenAI Math Becomes RL Environments: 369 Lean Proof Tasks on Hugging Face](/blog/openai-math-lean-rl-environments-hugging-face-harbor-369-tasks-2026)

   On October 11, 2026, Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue said OpenAI's math problems had been turned into open-source RL environments on the Hub. The dataset packages 369 Lean theorem-proving tasks for the Harbor framework, each graded by a separate proof checker. This guide explains how it works and what its strict reward can and cannot teach a model.
2. Oct 11

   [Sakana AI MASS: A 27B Model That Trains Itself Through Agent Teams](/blog/sakana-mass-multi-agent-self-supervision-recursive-self-improvement-2026)

   Sakana AI and UC Berkeley released MASS, a recursive self-improvement recipe where one open-weight 27B model runs a team of subagents, searches for better workflows, judges them itself, then trains on the winners. The gains are real but uneven, and the safety discussion is the interesting part.
3. Oct 10

   [Only 3.6% of 857 Chinese AI Model Releases Came With a Safety Result, SemiAnalysis Finds](/blog/china-ai-labs-safety-disclosure-857-releases-semianalysis-beijing-will-not-pace-the-frontier-2026)

   SemiAnalysis published a release census of nine Chinese AI labs: of 857 model releases from 2021 to September 15, 2026, only 31 ever had a developer-published safety result and 9 had one at launch. This post walks through the method, the lab-by-lab picture, the argument about Beijing and the pacing debate, and the limits of the data.
4. Oct 9

   [Ecosia Drops Mistral for Open-Weight Models: What Politico Reported and What It Means](/blog/ecosia-drops-mistral-open-weight-models-melious-politico-2026)

   Politico reported on October 6, 2026 that Ecosia is dropping Mistral as its AI model supplier and moving to open-weight models, some of them Chinese, hosted by Melious. The headline many people saw was a new Ecosia and Mistral partnership. The reporting says the opposite. This post separates the facts from the framing.
5. Oct 9

   [LightOnOCR-3: Apache 2.0 OCR in 0.8B, 1B and 4B, Ranked on ParseBench](/blog/lightonocr-3-parsebench-open-weight-ocr-2026)

   LightOn released LightOnOCR-3 on October 8, 2026. Three Apache 2.0 sizes read pages, return labeled bounding boxes, describe images and turn charts into tables. The company says the 4B and 0.8B lead open models on ParseBench. The public leaderboard tells a more mixed story.
6. Oct 9

   [Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo: The 8-Step 7B Image Model, and How to Run It](/blog/qwen-image-2-1-turbo-8-step-7b-open-checkpoint-diffusers-how-to-run-2026)

   Qwen has published Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, an accelerated checkpoint of its 7B Qwen-Image-2.1 that generates and edits images in 8 denoising steps with CFG set to 1. Here is how to run it, what the settings mean, and what the license allows.
7. Oct 9

   [Sakana Namazu Powers Aillis Evidence Finder: A Japanese LLM Scores 96.4% on the Physician Exam](/blog/sakana-namazu-aillis-evidence-finder-japanese-medical-llm-2026)

   On October 9, 2026, Sakana AI announced that its Japanese-focused LLM Sakana Namazu was adopted by Evidence Finder, a literature search tool for physicians from Aillis Inc. The Namazu-based evaluation model scored 96.4% on the 120th national physician exam, which Aillis says is the highest published score among GENIAC-designated domestic models. Sakana itself says an exam score is only one facet of usefulness.

   Tencent has published the weights of Youtu-Parsing-Omni, a compact 5B model that reads document pages, charts, geometry figures, audio and video and answers in one structured JSON envelope. explainx.ai walks through the benchmark table, how to run it, and the license clause to check first.

   SemiAnalysis, as relayed by the Financial Times, says China has more than 24 GW of operating data center capacity with roughly 50 GW more planned or announced, against about 56 GW in the US by the end of 2026. Gigawatts are not the same as compute, so here is how to read the figures.

It leads open models of its size in the company's own evaluation, trails a dense Qwen3.8 27B, and is built around a German tokenizer, German reasoning and trained abstention.
